text:
Alex: heads-up — saw a big drop in prefix/prompt cache hit-rate on Private clusters after the runtime bump last week. Hosted/Dedicated are mostly fine.
Maria: how big a drop? numbers? :thinking_face:
Alex: quick snapshot from yesterday: Hosted 72% hit, Dedicated 65% hit, Private 27% hit. these are aggregated over 24h for a ~1k qps customer.
Sam: wow that's huge. any obvious error logs? network timeouts?
Alex: not classic timeouts. Profiling suggests cache key mismatch + delayed warmup on Private (KV lookups returning miss then immediate write). Also noticed higher serialize latency when netstore is used via VPC mount.
Jules: could be config drift — we pushed netstore key-normalization change in runtime v176 that used xxhash64 in-process for keying, but netstore still expects SHA1-prefixed keys in some hosted configs.
Maria: do we have the patch diff? I can pull it.
Alex: pasted a small snippet of the key function we shipped:
```
# simplified pseudocode
def make_cache_key(prompt_prefix, user_id, seq_len):
    normalized = normalize_whitespace(prompt_prefix)
    hash = xxhash64(normalized)    # v176 change
    return f"kv:{user_id}:{seq_len}:{hash}"
```
Maria: ok that explains it. Private netstores (customers running our VPC package) still run an older netstore agent that canonicalizes keys with sha1 and lowercasing. mismatches = misses.
Sam: so Hosted/Dedicated had their netstore upgrade in step with runtime but Private fleets didn't get the agent update? config drift again.
Jules: yes — we rolled separate images for private customers and the image tag enforcement missed the agent bump. ops-bot shows last netstore-agent digest for private fleets is from 2025-11-03.
ops-bot: <@Jules> private-netstore: agent-digest v20251103 still present on 12/14 nodes.
Maria: besides keying mismatch, you mentioned warmup delays. what's up there?
Alex: batching heuristics changed too — new dynamic batcher delays small prefixes slightly hoping for more aggregation; on Private the extra RTT to netstore makes that delay longer, so we miss short-lived prefixes. netstore RTT: Hosted ~3ms, Dedicated ~6ms, Private (VPC mount via customer net) ~28–120ms depending on region.
Sam: longer RTT -> timer-based batcher waits hit SLOs -> fallback to synchronous path -> misses.
Jules: interesting interplay: kernel selection improvements reduced CPU for token loop, so tokens per-second increased, changing sequence length distribution, which changed how often prefixes re-hit before eviction. small cascading effect.
Maria: can we validate hypothesis with a repro? capture traces for a single customer on Private: kv.get latencies + cache miss reasons + batcher timer firings.
Alex: I ran a quick trace capture: attached summary lines here:
```
kv.get latency p50=32ms p95=110ms p99=240ms
cache.lookup: miss(reason=key-mismatch) 42%
cache.lookup: miss(reason=stale) 18%
batcher: timer-fired due_to_rtt 37% of small-prefix batches
```
Sam: nice. so two sources: 1) key encoding drift (xxhash vs sha1) 2) higher netstore RTT interacting with batcher heuristics. both hit-rate killers.
Maria: proposed fixes: A) revert the keying change in runtime and ship a compatibility shim that checks both hashing schemes for a short window. B) add normalization shim in netstore-agent so older agents can accept xxhash keys by mapping/aliasing. C) tune batcher heuristics when netstore RTT > X ms (short-circuit timer). D) add a canary metric for cache-key-version to detect drift early.
Jules: I like compatibility shim + agent update. revert would be too risky long term. shim idea: try primary key, if miss then try legacy key and warm forward into store (atomic). cheap and quick.
Sam: micro-runbook: 1) patch runtime to try legacy key on miss and write canonical new key on hit (low-risk). 2) ship netstore-agent update for Private with normalization. 3) change batcher: if network-backend and p95_kv > 20ms then reduce timer target by 50% for small prefixes.
Alex: I'll open a PR for the runtime shim and include perf tests. also adding a debug flag to log when legacy-key fallback used (only for canary).
Maria: Ops: can we schedule private cluster upgrades for netstore-agent next week? Jules?
Jules: scheduling now — will prioritize customers impacted. will also add a script to detect mismatched agents across private fleets.
ops-bot: <@Maria> private-netstore-agents: upgrade window requested for 2026-03-24 02:00-06:00 UTC.
Sam: for observability, add these dashboards: cache-hit-rate by deployment-mode, kv.get p50/p95, batcher timer-firings, and cache-key-fallback-rate.
Alex: noted. I'll add an alert: if Private hit-rate < 50% for >10m then page eng-runtime.
Maria: follow-up task: run a synthetic workload that mimics PLG traffic to verify warmup improvement and ensure no regression in Hosted/Dedicated.
Jules: anything else?
Alex: one more: kernel selector tweak earlier increased token throughput but we should run ablations to check eviction patterns — will include that in the PR tests.
Sam: thanks everyone. can we list owners? Alex -> runtime shim PR, Maria -> perf test harness, Jules -> agent rollout, Sam -> batcher change + dashboards.
Maria: I'll kick off the perf runs and post results here. :rocket: 
Alex: thanks, will circle back with numbers tomorrow. :thumbsup:
